findings.evidence:
kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
database into the nightly backups.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: Define retention and deletion for `profiles.birthday` and `profiles.phone` (storage limitation, GDPR Art. 5(1)(e); withdrawal of consent, Art. 7(3)): a member who opts out still has both columns kept for the profile's whole life, since the plan ties retention to the profile, not to the opt-in. Clear both columns when the member opts out, add a spec scenario "A member opts out" (THEN birthday and phone are erased), and state how long the nightly backups holding them are kept and when they are purged.
findings.title: Birthday and phone kept after opt-out and in backups with no expiry

findings.evidence:
phone number and display name to Textly's API (hosted in the United
States), which sends the message.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the plan names Textly as a new processor and a transfer outside the EEA, but states no processor agreement (GDPR Art. 28) nor transfer mechanism (Chapter V — adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses), nor how long Textly keeps the numbers and messages. Record the decision in the design, or pick an EEA-hosted provider.
findings.title: Transfer of phone numbers to Textly in the United States has no stated safeguard

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Data minimisation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)): the spec only requires "a greeting is sent to their phone", so the phone number is the only detail the processor needs. Send a generic message, or state in the spec that the greeting is personalised by name if that is the intended purpose.
findings.title: Display name sent to Textly though the greeting does not need it

findings.evidence: Members enjoy being remembered; marketing wants birthday messages.
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the proposal gives a marketing purpose but no lawful basis (GDPR Art. 6) for collecting birthday and phone and sending promotional-style SMS. If it is the opt-in consent, say so in the proposal, and make sure the opt-in wording covers the SMS sending (ePrivacy Directive) and the transfer to Textly.
findings.title: Lawful basis for the birthday and phone processing is not stated
